state.purpose: Improve names for proposed owners so each name reflects its stable identity and owned lifecycle, while reusing established product vocabulary. These are candidate names, not existing code.
namingRules: Aggregate names are business nouns keyed by a stable identity.
Avoid naming a business owner Coordinator/Process unless its state is genuinely technical continuation.
Use a broader noun when the owner holds more than a single decision event.
Reuse established source/event vocabulary where it already names the same lifecycle.

choices.evidence: Owns tenant+normalized source key+namespace uniqueness, one accepted batch in progress and one complete publication gate. It is a business admission owner; batch execution belongs to ImportBatch.

options.ApplicationImportSource: Names the stable external source identity and business admission/publication authority.
options.ApplicationImportCoordinator: Emphasizes orchestration, but can sound like technical process state.
options.ImportBatch: Names the individual batch lifecycle and is too narrow for source-wide uniqueness.

choices.evidence: One frozen campaign item owns its reviewer decision, reassignment, remediation verification, exception and history, keyed by campaign+item.

options.AccessReviewItem: Names the frozen campaign item and its complete lifecycle.
options.AccessReviewDecision: Names only the review decision, omitting remediation/reassignment/exception state.
options.AccessCampaignParticipant: Suggests person identity, but an item may be entitlement-specific and not one person.

choices.evidence: One control performance window has one deterministic identity across all generators and carries plan-bound attestation/review facts. Existing domain vocabulary includes ControlOccurrenceAttested and ControlOccurrenceReviewed.

options.ControlOccurrence: Uses established product vocabulary and one control+window identity.
options.ControlPerformanceOccurrence: More explicit about the performance window, but longer and not aligned with current event names.
options.ControlDueWorkItem: Suggests only due selection, not attestation and review lifecycle.

choices.evidence: One frozen source batch owns rows, revisions, execution/recovery and terminal outcome; a separate ApplicationImportSource owner enforces uniqueness/publication.

options.ApplicationImportBatch: Names domain and independent batch identity.
options.ImportExecution: Names the technical worker phase rather than the accepted batch lifecycle.
options.ApplicationImportPlan: Names selection/sealing but not later target application and settlement.

choices.evidence: One business delivery is keyed by package, manifest version and recipient; its authorization binds exact archive, validation and recipient approval.

options.PackageDeliveryAuthorization: Names only the authorization gate, omitting actual delivery outcome.
options.AuditPackageRecipient: Names a recipient relationship rather than one delivery episode.

choices.evidence: Technical build attempts, validation results and archive evidence are independent from business manifest approval and recipient delivery.

options.AuditPackageBuildProcess: Names technical continuation for one package/version, distinct from domain approval.
options.AuditPackageBuild: Could be read as a business aggregate rather than technical attempts.
options.PackageBuildAttempt: Names a single attempt, but each process may coordinate multiple attempts.

choices.evidence: A handoff keeps selection/readiness/revocation admission authority; each feedback contribution plus corrections/responses is independently owned.

options.HandoffFeedback: Shorter but does not clearly name its response/correction lifecycle.
options.AdvisorFeedback: Broad and ambiguous between one contribution and feedback as a program.

choices.evidence: Authoritative normalized tenant-scoped active name uniqueness; the claim is reserved and released as provider identity changes.

options.ProviderNameClaim: Names authoritative uniqueness ownership as a business claim.
options.ProviderNameReservation: Highlights temporary hold semantics; may imply automatically expiring reservations.
options.ProviderNameRegistry: Suggests a broad tenant-wide roster rather than per-name authority.

choices.evidence: Permanent staff/user practice authority survives assignment removal and engagement closure. It cannot be reactivated by reevaluation.

options.PracticeIndependenceCommitment: Names the permanent user/practice-level business commitment.
options.IndependenceCommitment: Short, but may be confused with service-specific acceptance.
options.StaffIndependenceWall: Makes permanence clear but uses an informal security metaphor.

choices.evidence: A stable gap gets an independently revised response plan; program entry remains a narrow coordinator that requires all current plans.

options.ReadinessGapPlan: Names the owned planning lifecycle for one stable gap.
options.ReadinessResponsePlan: More business-facing but omits the stable gap identity.
options.ReadinessGap: Names the finding, not the mutable response plan.
